description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:804–853

Two helpers exist with opposite error semantics:
- find_cert_ext: fail-open (silently drops DER errors)
- try_find_cert_ext: fail-closed (propagates DER errors)

The doc-comment on each helper explains its own behaviour well. The concern is at the call sites:

- BasicConstraints uses find_cert_ext (fail-open): line 856
- NameConstraints uses cert_name_constraints which calls try_find_cert_ext (fail-closed): line 877
- CertificatePolicies uses find_cert_ext (fail-open): line 1588
- PolicyMappings uses find_cert_ext (fail-open): line 1785
- PolicyConstraints uses find_cert_ext (fail-open): lines 1739, 1904
- InhibitAnyPolicy uses find_cert_ext (fail-open): line 1919

The asymmetry between BasicConstraints (fail-open) and NameConstraints (fail-closed) is intentional and well-motivated (NC is security-critical; a malformed NC could be used to widen constraints, so fail-closed is correct). However this distinction is not documented at the call site for BasicConstraints.

A future maintainer refactoring cert_basic_constraints to use try_find_cert_ext for 'consistency' would introduce a regression: a cert with malformed BasicConstraints DER would fail with MalformedCertificate instead of being treated as a non-CA. The current fail-open behaviour is correct for BC (malformed BC → treated as no constraint present → cert fails the cA=TRUE check for a different reason). Add a comment to cert_basic_constraints explaining why fail-open is the correct choice here.
title: find_cert_ext/try_find_cert_ext asymmetry not documented at call sites
